blocks.intro: In a town full of family kitchens, disposals work hard.

items.body: A disposal installed with a 1990s or 2000s home is probably on borrowed time. Most last about 8 to 15 years.
A kitchen remodel is a good time for a quieter, more powerful unit.
Slow draining often means grease in the line behind the disposal. We check it.
In most kitchens, the dishwasher drains through the disposal. A clogged disposal can make the dishwasher back up too, so we check both.

blocks.h2: Garbage Disposal Questions From Algonquin Homeowners

items.q: How do I reset my garbage disposal?
items.preview: Press the red button on the bottom.
items.answer: Turn off the switch, wait a minute, then press the red reset button on the bottom of the unit. If it still won't run, call us.

items.preview: Jams and loose connections are repairs. A leaking body or dead motor means replace.
items.answer: Jams, a tripped reset and loose connections can be fixed. A leaking housing or burned-out motor means a new unit.

items.q: What shouldn't go down the disposal?
items.preview: Grease, bones, fibrous scraps, coffee grounds, eggshells, rice and pasta.
items.answer: Grease and oil, bones, fibrous scraps, coffee grounds, eggshells, rice and pasta.

items.q: What size disposal should I get?
items.preview: Bigger motors handle family cooking better.
items.answer: For a busy family kitchen, a unit with a stronger motor handles more and jams less. We'll recommend one that fits your sink.

items.q: Is a louder disposal a sign it's failing?
items.preview: Often. Worn bearings or loose parts get noisier.
items.answer: Often. A disposal that gets noticeably louder or rattles may have worn bearings or a loose mount. If it's also leaking or jamming, replacement is usually the better value.

items.q: What does disposal replacement cost in Algonquin?
items.preview: It depends on the unit. The price comes first.
items.answer: It depends on the unit and any plumbing or electrical changes. We quote a flat rate before we start.
